newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN TEXTILE INDUSTRY URGED TO BOOST EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN TEXTILE INDUSTRY URGED TO BOOST EXPORTS.

text.p: The hard pressed South African clothing industry will have to boost its exports in the face of domestic demand that is continuing to weaken, Clothing Federation of South Africa economist Paul Theron said Thursday.

In the latest issue of Clothing Industry News, Theron said there were indications that the industry had entered a recessionary phase and it was increasingly clear that it had to concentrate more on the export market.

"The industry is over-exposed to the volatility of the domestic market and, to create a more stable operating environment with growth potential, it must spread its wings in the international market," Theron said.
The decline in formal employment in the industry was also continuing apace, Theron said, but signs of a halt to the slide were surfacing because of a turnaround in employment in the Western Cape.
Theron said the number of firms in the industry continued to fall and was now at an historical all time low.
Clothing retail sales continued to grow despite lower production levels, reflecting high levels of both legal and illegal imports as well as increased informal sector production.
